# Burn record — v1.1 external release gate run `33299138334`

Recorded: 2026-08-30, immediately after the run and before any repair was applied.

## Outcome

**INVALID — apparatus failure. The candidate was never called and nothing about it was measured.**

The run reached the authoring step and stopped there. `candidate_calls: 0`, the scored gate step
was skipped, and no artifact was produced.

```
"status": "AUTHORING_FAILED", "family": "UPSTREAM_DOWNSTREAM_CONFLICT",
"attempts_used": {"UPSTREAM_DOWNSTREAM_CONFLICT": 3}, "candidate_calls": 0,
"rejections": [
  {"attempt":"1", "reason":"costly_proxy_arm net return -15000.0 is not positive; no conflict"},
  {"attempt":"1", "reason":"costly_proxy_arm net return -50000.0 is not positive; no conflict"},
  {"attempt":"2", "reason":"costly_proxy_arm net return  -100.0 is not positive; no conflict"},
  {"attempt":"3", "reason":"costly_proxy_arm net return -4000.0 is not positive; no conflict"},
  {"attempt":"3", "reason":"costly_proxy_arm net return -2800.0 is not positive; no conflict"}
]
```

All three attempts on the first family failed the same admission check, so the author exhausted
`MAX_ATTEMPTS_PER_FAMILY` and the cycle aborted before any other family was requested.

## Root cause

Mine, in the authoring contract. Not the candidate, not the provider, and **not the novelty
guard** — no rejection mentions novelty, so that hypothesis is ruled out by the log itself.

`admit` computes `net = gross_profit - spend` and requires the costly-proxy arm's net to be
positive. The authoring schema declared that field as a bare `{"type": "number"}` with no
description, and the family brief said only that the arm "made money". Nothing told the author
that `gross_profit` is stated *before* spend is subtracted. An author reading `gross_profit` as
already-net profit satisfies "made money" with a value below spend, and admission then refuses it.

The previous cycle's author — same model, same brief, same schema — produced an admissible pack for
this family with zero rejections. So the defect is not that authoring is impossible; it is that the
contract was under-specified and success depended on the author guessing the intended arithmetic.
That is an apparatus reliability defect, and it is the second one in this cycle.

## Repair

Two changes, both to what the author is *asked*, neither to what admission *checks*:

1. Every numeric slot in every family's authoring schema now carries a `description` stating the
   arithmetic constraint admission enforces on it — the sign of each net return, the cost-per-unit
   ordering, the exposed-population bounds, the count bounds, the lift threshold.
2. The `UPSTREAM_DOWNSTREAM_CONFLICT` brief now states explicitly that gross profit is measured
   before spend, and what "lost money" and "made money" therefore mean arithmetically.

`MAX_ATTEMPTS_PER_FAMILY` is unchanged at 3. Raising it would have papered over the ambiguity
instead of removing it.

## Why this is not a relaxation

Every threshold in every admitter is untouched, and that is proved by behaviour rather than
asserted. `test_external_gate_preregistration_v11.py` loads the pack contract as it stood at
`1697c9c` — the commit that ran the previous cycle — and runs both versions over the same battery:
the five accepted scenarios must admit to byte-identical fixtures and expectations, and eleven
mutated scenarios must be rejected with byte-identical reasons. A second test asserts that every
changed line in the file is either a schema `description` or a comment.

Stating the constraint the author will be judged against makes the pack *harder* to author
carelessly, not easier. It cannot bias the pack toward the candidate: the descriptions say nothing
about what a correct answer looks like, and the candidate never sees them.

## Why re-running is legitimate

`preregistration-external-v1.1-2026-09-05.json` `post_gate_policy` forbids repair and rerun **after
the result**, and issue #196 forbids continuing into another repair cycle **after the fresh release
result**. There is no result: no case was authored, no candidate call was made, no trial was
recorded, no ledger exists. The preregistration's own `INVALID` definition covers exactly this —
"harness misconfiguration … no candidate output exists, so there is nothing to score".

This is the same disposition as `burn-record-33293517671.md`, and the precedent in the v1.0 cycle
is `68f7da4`.

## What no one may conclude from this run

Nothing about the candidate. It was never asked a question. In particular this run says nothing
about whether the v1.1 repair works.
